text.p: SME - The European Union (EU) on Monday repeatedly called for the government to respect democratic principles and improve democratic standards in Slovakia. Dutch Charge d'Affairs to Slovakia, Hugo Gajus Scheltema, presented the statement at the EU-Slovak joint parliamentary committee which is currently meeting in Bratislava.
NARODNA OBRODA - Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski will pay a two-day visit to Slovakia, starting on July 17.
- Slovakia still insists on the return of 4.12 tonnes of gold from former Czechoslovak reserves, currently held in Prague.
- Both Slovakia and the Czech Republic said they would agree on withdrawing claims against each other related to the split of former Czechoslovakia.

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic has called an extraordinary session of parliament on June 19. The session was called by opposition deputies in an attempt to dismiss Interior Minister Gustav Krajci.

- Frantisek Gaulider, a former deputy for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), has appealed to the human rights court in Strasbourg against the withdrawal of his parliamentary mandate last autumn.
- The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said it considered expulsion of Slovakia from the first wave of NATO enlargement as a success of its policy.
- Overall debts of state-run Slovak Railways (ZSR) now total some 5.1 billion crowns.

- The government is expected to discuss the transformation of state-owned Slovak Telecom to a state-run joint-stock company at its regular session on Tuesday. The government is also due to discuss state guarantees for loans planned in 1997.

PRAVDA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Monday the recent run on the crown was not only an attack by foreign speculators, but that domestic subjects have also played on the depreciation of the currency.
- NBS Vice-governor Marian Jusko said the central bank expected interbank rates to return to their levels under 20 percent but he would not elaborate when this should happen.
